threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal for a pub to serve breakfast at 10am. Everyone knows it's brunch or nothing, mate.
Heard a guy on the 196 bragging about how he can smuggle a whole pizza into the club. No one batted an eye, just another night in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last summer, I saw a guy on his balcony watering his plants while barbecuing sausages. Gotta love the multitasking spirit of Neukölln!

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Turkish bakery open at 3 AM serving fresh simit while the pink dawn breaks over the Spree. Pure magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they seamlessly navigate the BART delays; they don't panic, just pull out a book and settle in.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a woman in the Tenderloin serenading the bus stop crowd with her guitar, not a soul seemed to mind the delay. Just another day in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think the park is just for picnicking. Most locals come for the dodgeball games and impromptu dance sessions after dark.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confused look when the tram goes past without stopping—still thinking it’s a bus.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of just 'the Overground.' Everyone else has already adapted to the clunky connections.
Heard a guy on the N35 boasting about his 'royal rum' stash while the bus jostled past the old cinema. Made me think, what's the craziest thing in a backpack?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was here when I saw a crowd laughing around an old man selling handmade soaps by the canal, weaving stories between his sales pitches.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous techno parties in abandoned buildings here. Not just clubs, real DIY vibes. It's an experience that’s hard to find elsewhere.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to skip the BART on Fridays; it's a mess with overheated brakes and delays. Tourists just fume in line.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy with a pet iguana on the Muni—he claimed it’s a service animal. Only in the Tenderloin would that get a nod from the driver.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think 'local' means a trendy brunch spot. In Gràcia, it's really about the neighborhood market where everyone knows your name.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You know they're new when they still stop to take selfies with the Gaudí buildings instead of just rolling their eyes.
